chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

"Ghusl is in seventeen situations; among them, three are obligatory." So I said: "May I be your ransom, which of them are obligatory?" He said: "The ghusl of janabah, the ghusl of one who has washed a deceased person, and the ghusl for ihram."
As for his statement, "and the ghusl for ihram," although according to us it is not obligatory, its meaning is that its reward is the reward of an obligatory ghusl.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: the consecrated state entered for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath performed for purification in specific religious contexts
key_terms.الْفَرْضُ: that which is obligatory or legally required
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after the state of janabah

ai.seo_question: Which types of ghusl are obligatory according to this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the rulings of ghusl and states that there are seventeen occasions for ghusl, of which three are identified as obligatory in the report. It then clarifies that the ghusl for ihram, though mentioned among them, is understood in this source as carrying the reward of an obligatory ghusl rather than being legally obligatory itself.
